fields.statement: At 8e8c092d I built rhiza with go build -trimpath and walked docs/quickstart.md by hand in a fresh scratch git repo (own HOME, RHIZA_* unset): git init, rhiza init, change new, rhiza add capability reports, add capability export-csv --parent reports, add decision csv-streaming with the quoted quote field, rhiza link export-csv decided-by csv-streaming, propose, accept, land, show, why, tree, render, check (ok), git commit. Every command succeeded. show export-csv lists decided-by csv-streaming, show csv-streaming keeps the quote verbatim, tree nests export-csv under reports, why lists the decision and the landed change set. The page's rhiza set mention works too: set export-csv --field ... --dry-run then real updated the statement. grep finds no {"writes in the page; rhiza apply gets one sentence. go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/quickstart passes.

At 8e8c092d README.md no longer says pages are on the way (grep finds no 'on the way' in README.md or docs/quickstart.md). Its Where next links the quickstart, concepts (model, change-sets, why), agents, runs-and-daemon, custom-workflows and the generated reference (cli, config, workflow-file); every target file exists. go test -trimpath ./internal/doclinks/... passes, and make self-check in a clean detached worktree at HEAD prints ok (in the run checkout it fails only on this QA session's own untracked actor record). The owner's approval is left to sign-off.

At 8e8c092d grep -n -i rise-ah README.md matches line 3, the opening paragraph under # Rhiza where the name is introduced: Rhiza (it's said rise-ah) keeps a living model... The owner's approval is left to sign-off.
